ISTPF Orientation Public Schedule – 2026 All Times Mountain ISTPF 2026 Orientation Schedule Monday, August 31, 2026 2:00-4:30PM MDT Science and Technology Policy—History and Organization Dr. Anna Quider, Principal, The Quider Group Overview of the history, organization, and uses of science and technology policy in the United States, including the role of the White House, Congress, and federal agencies, as well as connection to Idaho. Registration required: https://uidaho.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_oFm9FpwTRtyvDnMUdwAPMg Tuesday, September 1, 2026 8:30-10:00AM MDT Idaho’s Political History Dr. Sarah Robey, Associate Professor of History, Idaho State University Dr. Stephanie Witt (Invited), Professor, Public Policy & Administration and Professor, Political Science, School of Public Service, Boise State University Introduction to Idaho’s geography and development, connecting to politics in Idaho from the historical perspective, touching on the three branches of government, important influencers, pivotal moments, local-state/state-federal dynamics, and more. Registration required: https://uidaho.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_Y-6SsNa1RRqI-6qmOYwciQ 1:30-2:45PM MDT Panel—Political Savviness State and federal science and technology policy fellows, current and alumni Transitioning from your lab or office to an agency may be a culture shift. Hear insights into how to navigate agency and government structures, understand quickly the policy process, ask for help in your new environment, and office and agency life. Registration required: https://uidaho.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_KsH5E5mDQw-q4DlK4000_A Wednesday, September 2, 2026 9:00-11:00AM MDT How a Bill Becomes a Law and Different Routes to Policy Jared Tatro, Team Lead, Impact Review Team, Idaho Legislative Services Office Brian Kane, Dean, College of Law, University of Idaho The basics of how a bill becomes a law, rules, statutes, policies, the role of courts, process of promulgating regulations, and constitutional amendments and bonds that are vital to policy. Registration required: https://uidaho.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_cqB0WPjIRkS-26c_K-Btmw Thursday, September 3, 2026 1:00-2:15PM MDT Panel—How to Successfully Brief State and federal science and technology policy fellows, current and alumni How do you successfully write talking points for yourself and others? What does it mean to brief your boss? How does an oral briefing connect to a written brief? Learn insights and best practices. Registration required: https://uidaho.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_s4PCDZAGSl62DBXbwl9AVg
